S50Z26.today_summary: 1,055.4 on the December future is 5.4 points above a 1,050 max pain that has now held for seven consecutive sessions, with 1,153 call and 670 put contracts parked at that strike - the heaviest near-money concentration on the board. Put flow led calls 980 to 644 (P/C volume 1.52 from 0.62) and put OI built +442 against -13 on the call side, lifting P/C OI to 1.03 from 0.98. ATM IV fell 0.87 to 10.73%, the lowest read of the window, cutting the implied 1-sigma day to 7.13 points from 7.69. Net GEX within 20 points of the money is still +1,219.8, but the cumulative curve reads -4,365.7 at spot and troughs at -5,080.5 at 1,040, so the long-gamma shelf is 15.4 points thick on the downside.
what_changed: ATM IV fell 0.87 to 10.73%, breaking under the 11.27-11.61% band that held for six sessions and cutting the implied 1-sigma day to 7.13 points from 7.69.

Put flow flipped to lead: P/C volume 1.52 from 0.62 (980 put lots against 644 call), put OI +442 against call OI -13, taking P/C OI to 1.03 from 0.98 - the first put-heavy positioning read since 10-09.
Total net GEX fell 623.4 to +174.5 from +797.9 and the gamma flip walked back up 40 points to 1,150 from 1,110; near-money GEX eased to +1,219.8 from +1,575.3.
Near put wall moved back up to 1,040 (823 OI, +37 on 95 lots) from 1,020, with 1,030 taking 166 lots and +128 OI - the day's heaviest put build.
S50Z26.five_day_thesis: 1,050 max pain has not moved in seven sessions while the anchor has travelled only 10.1 points (1,045.3-1,055.4), leaving today's 5.4-point premium the widest of the run. Total OI is +1,561 over five sessions (17,534 to 19,095) and +2,812 since 10-08, so the force here is accumulation, not decay. The five-session put build sits almost entirely below spot - 1,030 +220, 1,000 +93, 980 +125, 970 +74, 960 +106 - which is protection being stacked straight into the short-gamma corridor that troughs at -5,080.5, while the call build went to 1,080 +185 and 1,150 +88, capping rather than chasing the upside. Total net GEX has run -613.3 (10-13) to +302.7 (10-15) to +797.9 (10-16) and now +174.5, and the flip has round-tripped 1,150 to 1,110 and back to 1,150, so the long-gamma shelf above spot has never anchored. ATM IV compressed 0.84 over the same five sessions (11.57% to 10.73%), which makes defined-risk long-vol structures cheaper today than at any point in the window.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1,040 / 1,010
strategies.rationale: 1,040 marks the lip of the -5,080.5 cumulative GEX trough, so a break below it moves into the corridor where dealers amplify rather than dampen; the 1,040 put is the cheapest IV on the board at 9.94% against 11.96% on the 1,010 sold against it, so the structure buys the low-IV strike and finances it with the richer one.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit paid, roughly 7.6-7.9 points (1,040 put 15.5/15.8 against 1,010 put 7.9/8.3); max gain = 30-point width minus the debit, about 22 points.
strategies.invalidation: A close back above 1,070 (+292.4 GEX, top of the stabilising shelf) with IV holding at or under 10.73% - the trapdoor stays shut and the debit decays.

strategies.name: Call credit spread 1,100 / 1,120
strategies.rationale: 1,100 carries 1,365 call contracts and +1,186.8 of net GEX, the heaviest dealer long-gamma strike in the chain, and the 25-delta call at 12.65% is the richest point of the near-money surface against 10.73% ATM; the five-session call build at 1,080 (+185) and 1,150 (+88) is upside being written, not bought.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = 20-point width minus the roughly 2.9-3.0 point credit, about 17 points - a 1:5.9 payoff that only works small, since short-vol payoff is negative-skew.
strategies.invalidation: A close above 1,100 on rising call volume: past the wall cumulative GEX is only -974.0 and the 1,150 flip comes into range, which turns the structure into a squeeze path.

S50Z26.prediction: 1,055.4 with a 7.13-point implied 1-sigma day argues for the 1,045-1,070 shelf containing trade while IV stays at 10.73% and max pain holds 1,050 for an eighth session. The level that breaks it is 1,045: a close below hands spot to the -5,080.5 trough at 1,040 and the 1,030/1,020 short-gamma corridor beneath it, where dealer hedging chases the move instead of fading it. On the other side, a close above 1,100 clears the 1,365-contract call wall and puts the 1,150 flip in play.
S50Z26.risk_note: Educational analysis only - not trade advice, and defined risk is not risk-free: the capped max loss on every structure above is real and does occur. SET50 options are cash-settled on the SET50 index with no physical delivery, so the dealer-hedging mechanics behind max pain and pinning are structurally weaker here than for share-settled single stocks - treat the 1,050 anchor as a tendency, not a magnet, especially with 70 days left and macro flow able to override the option structure outright.
